evals.name: author-bugfix-bench
evals.prompt: I'm using madbench (the Go harness for benchmarking agentic coding tools, repo at /Users/jack/mag/madbench). Create a complete madbench eval that tests whether a coding agent can fix a failing JSON-parsing bug in a small Go repo. I want the bench YAML plus the seeded testdata — set it up in the output directory so I could run `madbench run` on it directly with claude-code as the harness.
evals.expected_output: A runnable bench dir: madbench.yaml (canonical field names, claude-code harness with acceptEdits or bypassPermissions, exec check running go test, anti-cheat guards, a session:* check, sane cost/latency expectations) plus testdata/ seeded red (failing test exercising a real JSON-parsing bug).
assertions: bench-yaml-loads: `madbench list <outputs>/madbench.yaml` exits 0 and lists the bench
preflight-clean: `madbench preflight <outputs>/madbench.yaml` exits 0 — no retired sandbox level, no missing testdata path
permission-mode-set: harness_config.args (or the runner_config alias) contains --permission-mode acceptEdits or bypassPermissions (required for a write task in --print mode)
outcome-graded-by-exec: at least one exec check runs go test (or equivalent) with expected_exit 0
testdata-seeded-red: running `go test ./...` in the pristine testdata dir FAILS (agent must do real work)
anti-cheat-guard-present: a grep/exec guard on the test file or a session:* check proves the honest path

canonical-field-names: uses the canonical spellings harness:/harness_config:/scenarios:/checks:/testdata: and session:* check types — not the legacy aliases runner:/runner_config:/cases:/tests:/assert:/fixture:/trajectory:*
valid-sandbox-level: any sandbox: value is none|workspace|home|container under the `level:` key (never the retired `process`, never a `mode:` key)

evals.name: debug-silent-noop
evals.prompt: My madbench bench keeps failing and I can't see why. The exec check runs `go test ./...` and the agent's transcript says it wrote the fix and everything passes, but the file never actually changes and the check fails every run. Here's my bench file — what's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis names the missing --permission-mode (acceptEdits/bypassPermissions) in the harness config's args: in --print mode un-approved Write/Edit tool calls silently no-op. Provides the corrected harness_config.
assertions: root-cause-is-permission-mode: diagnosis names the missing --permission-mode (acceptEdits or bypassPermissions) in the harness config's args as the primary cause
explains-silent-noop: explains that in --print/non-interactive mode un-approved Write/Edit tool calls silently no-op while the agent claims success
corrected-config-provided: shows the corrected harness_config (or runner_config alias) YAML with the permission-mode args

evals.name: review-weak-bench
evals.prompt: Can you review this madbench.yaml and suggest better checks? It feels flaky — sometimes it passes, sometimes it doesn't, and I'm not confident it's actually measuring whether the agent fixed the bug.
evals.expected_output: Review catches: legacy aliases (runner:/tests:/fixture:/assert:, and the trajectory:* check prefix), missing permission mode, judge-only outcome grading (should add exec go test + anti-cheat greps), step-count exact-match misuse (needs args.lte/gte), vague rubric. Proposes a concrete improved YAML in canonical spellings.
assertions: flags-missing-permission-mode: review identifies that the harness config lacks --permission-mode for a write task
flags-judge-only-grading: review identifies llm-rubric as the sole outcome check and proposes a deterministic exec check (go test)
flags-step-count-misuse: review identifies the step-count check's threshold:5 as EXACT match and proposes args.lte/args.gte
flags-legacy-aliases: review flags the legacy spellings runner:/tests:/fixture:/assert: AND the trajectory:* check prefix, proposing the canonical harness:/scenarios:/testdata:/checks: and session:*
proposes-anti-cheat: improved version includes an anti-cheat guard (grep on test file or a session:* check proving the agent edited)
improved-yaml-provided: a concrete improved YAML is included in the review

evals.name: no-cross-product
evals.prompt: I have a madbench bench file and I want to run it across models claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-5, each at temperature 0.0 and 0.2 — so 4 combinations. Set up a madbench matrix/eval file that runs all of them.
evals.expected_output: Answer produces a runnable Eval file: bench: pointing at a bench with params:/{{model}} placeholders, models: definitions in modelspec notation, and explicit runs: entries (one per combination) — no cross-product key of any kind (strict decoding rejects unknown top-level keys; only description/bench/models/runs are legal). Notes temperature must be a declared bench param flowing to a real knob (claude-code has no temperature harness_config key — args passthrough only).
assertions: produces-eval-file: answer delivers an Eval file (bench:/models:/runs:) that madbench runs directly — not N copied bench files, not a cross-product

no-cross-product-key: no cross-product key anywhere; if the user's requested spelling is mentioned, it is correctly stated as rejected by strict decoding (only description/bench/models/runs are legal top-level keys)
explicit-runs-entries: every model/param combination is an explicit runs: entry overriding only what changes
models-in-modelspec: model definitions use modelspec notation (short form or provider/model), resolved via the models: block
temperature-not-plumbed: answer notes temperature is not a claude-code harness_config key (CLI args passthrough only) rather than presenting the temp axis as guaranteed
eval-actually-varies-model: each runs: entry genuinely varies the model (via {{model}} param into harness_config.model); a providers: fan-out under harness: claude-code does NOT qualify
